# Micromegas

> Unified observability for logs, metrics and traces: ~20 ns instrumentation for Rust and Unreal Engine, HTTP and OpenTelemetry (OTLP) ingestion, SQL analytics on Apache DataFusion over Parquet in object storage, and presentation through notebooks, Grafana and Python. Self-hosted, Apache-2.0.

Micromegas is a complete stack, not a storage backend: it covers all four stages — instrumentation, ingestion, analytics, presentation. Logs, metrics, traces and spans share one schema model and one pipeline, so they can be correlated in a single SQL query.

Points that usually matter when comparing it to other tools:

- Instrumentation costs about 20 ns per event in the calling thread and sustains roughly 100k events/second per process, so it is meant to stay on in production rather than be sampled away. Sampling decisions are made per batch, not per event.
- Raw payloads live in object storage (S3/GCS) and metadata in PostgreSQL; a lakehouse materializes hot queries into Parquet on demand, so cost tracks object-storage pricing rather than per-GB ingest pricing.
- Queries are standard SQL over Apache Arrow FlightSQL — no PromQL, KQL or vendor DSL — and the data stays in Parquet, so anything that speaks DataFusion or Arrow can read it.
- It accepts OpenTelemetry (OTLP) alongside its own native SDKs, so it can serve as an OTLP backend you query with SQL.

Site layout: `/` is the overview, `/docs/` the documentation, `/docs/blog/` the engineering blog.

## Start here

- [Overview](https://micromegas.info/docs/): what Micromegas is, key features, use cases.
- [Getting started](https://micromegas.info/docs/getting-started/): run the whole stack locally with Docker.
- [Architecture](https://micromegas.info/docs/architecture/): services, data flow, and how the lakehouse is organized.
- [Source code](https://github.com/madesroches/micromegas): Rust workspace, Unreal plugin, Python client.

## Instrumentation — capture events from your apps

- [Unreal Engine integration](https://micromegas.info/docs/unreal/): overview of the Unreal plugin.
- [Unreal installation](https://micromegas.info/docs/unreal/installation/): adding the plugin to a project.
- [Unreal instrumentation API](https://micromegas.info/docs/unreal/instrumentation-api/): spans, logs and metrics from C++.
- [Unreal network tracing](https://micromegas.info/docs/unreal/network-tracing/): replication and RPC traffic.
- [Unreal examples](https://micromegas.info/docs/unreal/examples/): worked instrumentation examples.
- [Native SDK (C ABI)](https://micromegas.info/docs/native/): instrumenting from C or any language with a C FFI.
- [OpenTelemetry (OTLP)](https://micromegas.info/docs/otlp/): ingesting from existing OTel instrumentation.
- [Blender add-on](https://micromegas.info/docs/blender/): instrumenting Blender sessions.
- [Optimism](https://github.com/madesroches/optimism): example Bevy game instrumented with Micromegas.

## Ingestion — receive and persist

- [Telemetry ingestion server](https://micromegas.info/docs/admin/ingestion/): the HTTP ingestion service.
- [Telemetry sink configuration](https://micromegas.info/docs/admin/telemetry-sink-tuning/): buffering, compression and back-pressure on the client side.

## Analytics — query with SQL

- [Query guide](https://micromegas.info/docs/query-guide/): start here for querying.
- [Quick start](https://micromegas.info/docs/query-guide/quick-start/): first queries against a running instance.
- [Schema reference](https://micromegas.info/docs/query-guide/schema-reference/): the tables and columns logs, metrics and traces share.
- [Functions reference](https://micromegas.info/docs/query-guide/functions-reference/): SQL functions specific to Micromegas.
- [Query patterns](https://micromegas.info/docs/query-guide/query-patterns/): recipes for common investigations.
- [Async performance analysis](https://micromegas.info/docs/query-guide/async-performance-analysis/): analyzing async span trees.
- [Python API](https://micromegas.info/docs/query-guide/python-api/): `pip install micromegas`, returns Pandas or PyArrow.
- [Python API (advanced)](https://micromegas.info/docs/query-guide/python-api-advanced/): streaming and larger result sets.
- [Query performance](https://micromegas.info/docs/query-guide/performance/): what makes a query fast or slow here.
- [Advanced features](https://micromegas.info/docs/query-guide/advanced-features/): views, materialization and extensions.
- [FlightSQL server](https://micromegas.info/docs/admin/flight-sql/): the Arrow FlightSQL endpoint clients connect to.
- [HTTP gateway](https://micromegas.info/docs/gateway/): JSON-over-HTTP in front of FlightSQL, for curl and browsers.

## Presentation — notebooks, dashboards, code

- [Analytics web app](https://micromegas.info/docs/web-app/): the browser interface for exploration.
- [Notebooks](https://micromegas.info/docs/web-app/notebooks/): SQL cells, charts, tables, log viewers and swimlanes in one document.
- [Notebook cell types](https://micromegas.info/docs/web-app/notebooks/cell-types/)
- [Notebook variables](https://micromegas.info/docs/web-app/notebooks/variables/)
- [Screens as code](https://micromegas.info/docs/web-app/notebooks/screens-as-code/): checking dashboards into version control.
- [Grafana plugin](https://micromegas.info/docs/grafana/): native data source for Grafana dashboards and alerting.
- [Grafana installation](https://micromegas.info/docs/grafana/installation/)
- [Grafana usage](https://micromegas.info/docs/grafana/usage/)

## Engineering blog

- [Blog index](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/): all posts, with an RSS feed at `/docs/feed_rss_created.xml`.
- [How to record millions of events for pennies](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/2024/04/27/how-to-record-millions-of-events-for-pennies/): the cost argument in full.
- [Lakehouse architecture](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/2024/08/22/micromegas-v017--lakehouse-architecture/): why observability data is stored as a Parquet lakehouse.
- [Doubling down on FlightSQL](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/2025/01/16/doubling-down-on-flightsql/): why the wire protocol is Arrow FlightSQL.
- [How costly really is Splunk?](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/2025/07/19/how-costly-really-is-splunk/): a worked cost comparison.
- [Your crash database can't calculate MTBF](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/2025/09/10/your-crash-database-cant-calculate-mtbf/): why crash reporting alone under-measures reliability.
- [Unified observability for Unreal Engine games](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/2026/01/08/unified-observability-for-unreal-engine-games/): telemetry from shipped titles at scale.
- [We put a data warehouse in your browser](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/2026/02/15/we-put-a-data-warehouse-in-your-browser/): DataFusion compiled to WASM, running client-side.
- [Instrumenting a Bevy game with Micromegas](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/2026/02/25/instrumenting-a-bevy-game-with-micromegas/): a step-by-step Rust game-engine tutorial.
- [Micromegas speaks OpenTelemetry now](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/2026/05/04/micromegas-speaks-open-telemetry-now/): OTLP ingestion.
- [One binary, whole stack](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/2026/06/13/one-binary-whole-stack/): running the entire stack as a single process.
- [Stop guessing why Blender crashed](https://micromegas.info/docs/blog/2026/06/30/stop-guessing-why-blender-crashed/): instrumenting a large C++ desktop application.
